month_in_review.title: June in Review
month_in_review.summary: The correction in the Hang Seng TECH Index during June was primarily driven by valuation compression and a rotation in investor positioning, rather than a deterioration in the underlying technology cycle. While the index experienced a broad-based pullback, performance within the sector remained differentiated. Traditional internet platforms, consumer technology, and electric vehicle supply chains faced greater pressure, whereas AI-related sectors, semiconductors, and companies benefiting from domestic technology substitution demonstrated relatively stronger resilience. Overall, June’s correction should not be interpreted as a loss of confidence in China's technology sector. Rather, it reflects a transition from pricing AI narratives to evaluating AI earnings delivery, with investors seeking greater evidence of sustainable profit growth.

drivers.title: Higher Interest Rate Expectations Weighed on Valuations
drivers.body: The primary driver of the correction was continued uncertainty surrounding earnings delivery. A more hawkish tone from the U.S. Federal Reserve in June pushed Treasury yields and U.S. dollar strength higher, placing additional valuation pressure on Hong Kong-listed growth stocks and tightening liquidity conditions for offshore Chinese equities.

drivers.title: Preference for Earnings Visibility and Cash Flow Certainty
drivers.body: Against a tighter liquidity backdrop, investors became increasingly selective, favouring companies with stronger cash flow generation, clearer earnings visibility, and more tangible order pipelines. Internet platform companies continued to face headwinds from promotional competition, AI investment spending, and a gradual consumer recovery, while electric vehicle and consumer hardware companies remained exposed to pricing pressure, inventory adjustments, and uncertain demand.

drivers.title: AI Exposure Increased but Requires Further Earnings Validation
drivers.body: The June index review added AI-related companies such as Zhipu and MiniMax, increasing the index's AI exposure. However, these additions are not yet sufficiently large to materially alter the overall index composition. Following the strong rally in AI-related stocks, investors have increasingly shifted their focus towards valuation sustainability, share unlocks, and the pace of commercialisation.

monitor.title: Q2 Earnings and Guidance
monitor.body: Q2 earnings results, particularly trends in advertising, e-commerce monetization, cloud services, and AI commercialization among platform companies, will be critical in determining the pace of valuation recovery.

monitor.title: Liquidity Conditions
monitor.body: Investors should continue to monitor U.S. interest rates, RMB exchange rate movements, Southbound capital flows, and Hong Kong equity risk premiums. A more sustained recovery in the Hang Seng TECH Index will likely require stabilisation in external liquidity conditions.

month_in_review.outlook: The June correction was primarily driven by short-term valuation compression and sector rotation, rather than a structural deterioration in the sector's fundamentals. Looking ahead, the sustainability of any recovery will depend on companies' ability to deliver earnings growth and on AI-related investments transitioning from thematic enthusiasm to tangible commercial and financial results.

company_news.title: NetEase (9999.HK) games’ Eggy Party PC version goes live
company_news.summary: NetEase Games’ party game Eggy Party launched on Windows, bringing the full experience to PC players with cross-platform account and data synchronization between mobile and PC. The PC version preserves popular game modes and introduces a PC-exclusive map editor. A Mac version is also currently in development.

company_news.title: SMIC (0981.HK) raises full-year outlook as domestic orders drive Q2 guidance well above consensus
company_news.summary: Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation reported first-quarter 2026 revenue of US$2.505 billion, up 0.7% sequentially. For Q2, the company guided revenue to US$2.86 billion to US$2.90 billion, implying quarter-on-quarter growth of 14% to 16%.

company_news.title: BYD (1211.HK) chairman says firm will be world’s biggest automaker in 5 years
company_news.summary: BYD chairman Wang Chuanfu said he expects the Chinese firm to become the world’s largest automaker within five years, as he sought to reassure investors following a steep decline in the company’s share price.

company_news.title: Meituan (3690.HK)’s reset starts with narrower delivery losses
company_news.summary: In the first quarter of 2026, Meituan recorded RMB 91 billion in revenue, up 5.6% year-on-year. Its operating loss narrowed to RMB 6.5 billion from RMB 16.1 billion in the previous quarter.

company_news.title: Baidu AI chip unit Kunlunxin targets US$50 billion valuation in Hong Kong IPO, report says
company_news.summary: Baidu's AI chip unit Kunlunxin is planning a Hong Kong IPO targeting a valuation of US$50 billion, pointing to renewed momentum in Hong Kong and China's technology fundraising.

company_news.title: Zhipu AI market cap tops HK$1 trillion as GLM-5.2 developer's shares soar
company_news.summary: Zhipu AI's market capitalisation surpassed HK$1 trillion after its Hong Kong-listed shares surged following the release of its open-source GLM-5.2 model.

company_news.title: MiniMax (0100.HK) plans China IPO as it eyes local rivals like DeepSeek
company_news.summary: MiniMax Group has begun preparations for a domestic initial public offering, according to a regulatory filing, as the fast-growing artificial intelligence startup challenges local rivals including DeepSeek.
